extracted.intended_audience: Authors, peer reviewers, and editors of Nature Communications
extracted.subtask_description: Journal policy describing Nature Communications' transparent peer review scheme: what peer review files contain, who is included, reviewer consent and anonymity rules, redaction and limitations, and how transferred manuscripts are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of policy (which papers are included)
rubrics_metrics.description: All primary research papers published in Nature Communications that are submitted from November 1, 2022 will have a corresponding peer review file containing the reviewer comments to the authors and the author rebuttal letters published alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all primary research submissions received from the stated date; earlier transitional arrangements (see historical opt-out) do not apply to submissions from Nov 1, 2022 onward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the peer review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review files will contain the full reviewer reports to authors and the author rebuttal letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review file includes reviewer comments directed at the authors and the authors' responses. It does not include confidential comments to editors, editorial correspondence, or internal editor discussions unless editors add explanations; any permitted redactions will be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer consent and opt-out at invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are informed of this initiative when invited to review and can decline to review the manuscript if they are not comfortable with their review being published. Acceptance to review is regarded as permission to release the reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer does not want their review published they should decline the invitation. By accepting an invitation, a reviewer is taken to have agreed to the potential publication of their report (subject to anonymity rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity / publication of reviewer names
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer names are not published. Unless reviewers sign the comments to the authors with their name, we will respect and maintain their full anonymity under all circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers who wish to be identified may sign their reports, and they can request their name be added to their comments at any point, up to and including receipt of a notification that the manuscript has been accepted in principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have the option to make confidential comments on the manuscript to the editor if they would like, although we would prefer that, in the interest of transparency, this is avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential comments to editors remain out of the published peer review file. Any substantive points that authors need to address in revision should be placed in the 'comments to the authors' section of the reviewer’s report rather than in confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of confidential data
rubrics_metrics.description: The only exception [to publishing full reports] is the disclosure of confidential data provided to editors or reviewers, which authors will be able to suggest for redaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may propose redactions of confidential information before publication of the peer review file; any redactions made will be explicitly noted in the peer review file so readers are aware material was removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferred manuscripts and previously-submitted reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript has been transferred to Nature Communications after peer review at another Nature journal, then we will receive those reviewer reports. However, these reports and the author responses to them will not be included in our peer review files, as those reports were submitted to the other journal without consent to potential publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only reviewer reports written for Nature Communications will be included in its peer review file. If the same reviewers later agree to review for Nature Communications, only their NC reports are included. Peer review files will note that a manuscript was previously peer reviewed elsewhere but will not name the other journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of peer review files (what they do not capture)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer reports are taken into consideration when the editorial team decides whether to accept, reject or ask for changes to a manuscript, but just reading the peer review reports will not necessarily give a reader the full picture of the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence between authors and editors, reviewer comments made confidentially to editors, and internal discussions between editors will remain confidential. A paper might be published against the advice of a reviewer if other (possibly confidential) feedback favours publication; peer review files may not fully capture such discussions though editorial explanations may sometimes be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision letters not currently published
rubrics_metrics.description: In this first step towards more transparency we are focusing on making available to all the scientific discussions between authors and reviewers. We hope to evaluate whether to open up the process further at a later stage, for example by also publishing our editorial decision letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At present editorial decision letters are not routinely published alongside the peer review file; the journal may review this policy in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical author opt-out during initial phase (2016–2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an initial phase, for papers submitted from January 2016 to November 2022, authors were given the opportunity to opt out of this scheme at the point of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a historical note explaining that earlier in the pilot period authors could choose not to publish peer review files; approximately 70% chose to publish. It does not change the rule for submissions from Nov 1, 2022 onward.
